title_ne: स्वास्थ्यकर्मी तथा स्वास्थ्य संस्थाको सुरक्षा सम्बन्धी (दोस्रो संशोधन) विधेयक, २०८३
summary:
The main purpose of the Security of Healthcare Workers and Health Institutions (Second Amendment) Bill, 2083 is to make health services regular, reliable, dignified and effective, to protect healthcare workers and health institutions from unexpected incidents and financial liabilities that may arise during medical treatment, to amend existing legal provisions to provide effective protection due to increasing attacks on healthcare workers and health institutions, and to define trainees or practicing staff so as to provide them security (Statement of Objects and Reasons, Page 1). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

Trainees or practical practicing students under Medical and Allied Sciences may submit an application to the committee attaching a temporary registration certificate or student identity card (Section 4, Subsection 1, Page 2). If found reasonable upon inquiry of the application, the committee shall register the name of such healthcare worker or health institution student in the prescribed register book and issue a certificate thereof in the prescribed format to the applicant (Section 4, Subsection 2, Page 2). The Ministry may, subject to this Act or rules made under this Act, make necessary guidelines, procedures or standards (Section 6, Page 2).

For committing an offence under clause (a) of Section 3, there shall be imprisonment from two years to five years and a fine from Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh (Section 5, Page 2). For committing an offence under clause (b), (c) or (c1) of Section 3, there shall be imprisonment up to three years and a fine up to Rs. 3 lakh (Section 5, Page 2). For committing an offence under clause (d), (e), (f) or (g) of Section 3, there shall be imprisonment up to one year and a fine up to Rs. 1 lakh (Section 5, Page 2). The provision on who imposes the fine, the right to appeal, its time limit, and the court are not stated in the bill (not stated in the bill).
